findings.title: require_explicit_e164 does not make the +91 inference unreachable; an explicit non-Indian code can send the OTP to a stranger
findings.problem: normalize_phone applies _INDIAN_MOBILE_RE (^[6-9]\d{9}$) to the DIGIT STRING at identity/customer.py:132, after the '+' has already been stripped. require_explicit_e164 proves the prefix then delegates digits, so any explicitly coded international number totalling 10 digits and starting 6-9 is rewritten: +6591234567 (Singapore) becomes +916591234567. The customer_phone_ownership OTP is then sent over WhatsApp to an unrelated real Indian subscriber, the shopper can never sign in, and a permanent never-deleted PHONE# reservation can be minted for a number nobody involved owns. The client agrees on the same wrong answer, so §9.2's byte-for-byte note is satisfied and still wrong.
findings.fix: Call the delegate with the inference disabled: identity.customer.normalize_phone(text, default_country=""). Traced both ways against lines 120-150: '6591234567' -> '+6591234567'; '919876543210' -> '+919876543210'. No shared-module edit, delegate still owns the 10-15 bound and still raises InvalidPhoneNumber. T-19 must add require_explicit_e164('+6591234567') == '+6591234567' plus a digits-preserved assertion over a table of explicit codes (+65, +971, +44, +1, +91).

findings.title: §12 step 7 breaks cart.tsx and checkout/status.tsx, the only two customer pages that call the cookie-authenticated endpoints, and neither is in scope
findings.where: §12 steps 5-7, §11.2 customerAuth.ts row, §11.1 customerSession.ts row, T-25
findings.problem: src/pages/cart.tsx:149 and src/pages/checkout/status.tsx:159 both gate on customerAuth.getSession() and send 'Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>'. After step 7 nothing writes sessionStorage, so getSession() returns null for everyone: every Checkout click redirects a signed-in shopper to /account/sign-in (which bounces them back - a silent loop), and /checkout/status reports 'unavailable' for every in-flight payment. Even with a session restored, both POSTs carry no X-WD-CSRF, so §4.6's method-derived gate answers 403 CSRF_REQUIRED, which §6.4 keeps out of requiresReauth and cart.tsx does not handle (it branches only on 401). Neither file is in owned paths, §11.2's changed list, or §11.1; the customerAuth.ts blast-radius cell names status.tsx and omits cart.tsx. T-25 does not name src/test/CartCheckout.test.tsx, which already pins this behaviour.
findings.fix: Either (1) keep getSession() working as a shim (non-null sentinel when the cookie flag is on) AND route both pages' fetch through customerSession.apiFetch so the CSRF header is attached - still an edit to two files outside owned paths, so name it as coordination; or (2) if those files cannot be touched this run, add C-13 (cart.tsx and checkout/status.tsx move onto customerSession.apiFetch) and GATE §12 step 7 on it exactly as step 5 is gated on C-12 at step 4a. Add src/test/CartCheckout.test.tsx plus a cookie-mode case to T-25, and stop implying step 7 is as benign as step 6.

findings.title: Session responses carry no cache directives, and the GET body contains the CSRF token
findings.where: §3 endpoint table, §4.2, §4.6 cache-trade subsection, §12 --verify list, T-27
findings.problem: GET /customer/session returns customerId, masked displayPhone and the live csrfToken, built through lambda_utils/response.py:cors_response, which emits only Content-Type and three CORS headers - no Cache-Control, no Pragma, no Vary (response.py:47-80). The response travels back through the CloudFront-fronted Amplify rewrite. §4.6 already admits the distribution's cookie handling is unknown and measures x-cache for HTML, but never asks the question on the API side. If /api/* is cached without varying on Cookie, one shopper's customerId and CSRF token can be served to another viewer; if the first fill was anonymous, every signed-in shopper gets a cached 401 with no server-side evidence.
findings.fix: Add a single _respond() builder in lambda_utils/customer_session.py (response.py is fleet-shared and DO-NOT-TOUCH) that updates the returned dict's headers with {'Cache-Control': 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, private', 'Pragma': 'no-cache', 'Vary': 'Cookie, Origin'} and is used by every success and refusal path, with _denied delegating to it. Extend T-11 to assert no-store on all eight routes; add to --verify that the live GET /api/customer/session 401 carries Cache-Control: no-store; extend --verify-cookie-transport to record x-cache for /api/customer/session with a documented FAIL when two different-cookie requests both report Hit.

findings.title: C-12 grants 63+ fleet functions unconditional UpdateItem on the table the design calls the authority for every ownership check
findings.problem: The foreign roles receive dynamodb:GetItem AND dynamodb:UpdateItem on CustomerSessionIndexTable with no condition, and §11.1.1 justifies it as 'the grant that must be wide leaks nothing'. That is a confidentiality claim and it holds; the integrity claim is absent and false. The row holds customerId, poolId, csrfTokenHash, absoluteExpiresAt, revokedAt and tokenSource, and §4.2/§10.2 both say that row authorises the request. Any fleet function can therefore rewrite customerId (IDOR one layer below authorize_resource), clear revokedAt (defeating the zero-latency kill switch §7.2 relies on), extend absoluteExpiresAt (all three §5.2 enforcements live in the session function and see no foreign write), or overwrite csrfTokenHash (Gate 1's server state). §12 step 4a asserts the positives and the two confidentiality negatives only, so a passing gate is consistent with all four.
findings.fix: Preferred option (b): grant the two foreign roles dynamodb:GetItem ONLY and let the session function own the idle clock, with customerSession.ts pinging GET /customer/session on page show and at most every 30 minutes (it already single-flights that call per tab) so a cart-only shopper does not idle out. This also deletes the §4.2 co-write exemption. Option (a) is a DynamoDB FGAC condition bounding dynamodb:Attributes to [sessionIdHash, idleExpiresAt, lastSeenAt] with dynamodb:ReturnValues NONE - documented but NOT verified in this account, so it must be proven by simulate-principal-policy on a disallowed attribute before being relied on. Either way §12 step 4a gains the write negative, and §11.1.1's 'leaks nothing' sentence must be rewritten to say what the grant can and cannot do.

findings.title: Where the Cognito Session lives is specified two ways, and its deletion has no granted permission
findings.problem: §4.2 puts cognitoAuthSession on CustomerSessionsTable 'deleted on completion', while §8.8 and §10.1 put the provider Session on an otp# row with a 10-minute TTL. §4.2's placement is impossible: no table-1 row exists during a challenge (step 7 creates it after the code verifies, which is the property T-29 asserts). The otp# reading is correct and exposes a second gap: otp# rows live in DownloadGrantsTable, where §11.1.1 grants GetItem, PutItem and UpdateItem and NO DeleteItem, so 'deleted on completion' is unimplementable - the same M19 shape in the same policy row.
findings.fix: Delete the cognitoAuthSession line from §4.2 table 1 and state in §8.8 step 4 that the provider Session lives only on the otp# row. Then pick the completion mechanism and make REQUIRED_PERMISSIONS match: either add ('dynamodb:DeleteItem', '<DownloadGrantsTable arn>') with a comment naming §8.8 step 6, or specify UpdateExpression='REMOVE cognitoAuthSession SET consumed = :true' with ConditionExpression='consumed = :false' (covered by the existing UpdateItem) and let TTL reap the husk. T-29 asserts that after a completed /customer/session no stored row holds the provider Session string.

findings.title: The new-customer WhatsApp send is the primary flow and is specified in four words
findings.where: §8.8 step 3, §11.1.1 lambda:InvokeFunction row, §10 send-failure row, M20
findings.problem: M20 is cited only for which ARN to grant. The site it cites (customer-registration/handler.py::_send_code) specifies much more, all load-bearing: phoneId=META_PHONE_NUMBER_ID, templateName=OTP_TEMPLATE_NAME ('wecare_otp' AUTHENTICATION), language=OTP_TEMPLATE_LANGUAGE, a two-component body whose button MUST be sub_type 'url' and NOT 'copy_code' (verified against the live WABA 2026-09-25, because Meta rejects copy_code on an AUTHENTICATION template), and a synthetic invoke event at path /wa-business/messages/send/template. A business-initiated message to a brand-new number has no open 24h window, so a free-form send fails outright and surfaces as 502 send_failed - which §9.3 has already decided must not be reported as 'not a WhatsApp number'. The primary new-shopper path would be dead on arrival. Five env keys are implied and none is named in expected_environment().
findings.fix: Extract _send_code into a new additive shared module lambda_utils/comms/whatsapp_otp.py::send_otp_template(e164, code, *, invoke) and have both customer-registration and the session function call it, so the Meta-verified component shape has exactly one home. Add SENDER_FUNCTION, META_PHONE_NUMBER_ID, OTP_TEMPLATE_NAME, OTP_TEMPLATE_LANGUAGE and the route path to expected_environment() and --verify. Extend T-29 to assert the invoke payload's templateName, language, both components and sub_type == 'url' (never copy_code) against a fake Lambda client.

findings.title: The copy contract names the wrong source of record, the wrong count, and an existing test it will break
findings.problem: The approved strings live in src/lib/signInMessages.ts, not in sign-in.tsx (whose MSG object re-exports them and says so). There are eight exports; SECTION_6_MESSAGES is seven and INCLUDES MISSING_CODE ('Include your country code, like +91.') while EXCLUDING NOT_ON_WHATSAPP. §9.3 lists seven rows plus the hint and never mentions MISSING_CODE, which sits in exactly the deliberately-unreachable state §9.3 documents at length for NOT_ON_WHATSAPP - omitting it is how it gets deleted as dead code. src/test/SignInMessages.test.tsx already pins all of this and asserts against the PAGE SOURCE TEXT (the signInMessages import line, a signInMessages.<KEY> reference per key, the no-red .si-error block), so §11.2's one-code rewrite of sign-in.tsx will trip it - and that file is named nowhere in the design. T-16 instead re-pins 'the seven live MSG strings' in AccountSignIn.test.tsx, duplicating an existing contract with the wrong count against the wrong source.
findings.fix: Name src/lib/signInMessages.ts as the authority in §9.3, add a MISSING_CODE row with its unreachable-by-construction status beside NOT_ON_WHATSAPP, and note SECTION_6_MESSAGES is seven INCLUDING MISSING_CODE. Add src/test/SignInMessages.test.tsx to §11.2 with the constraint that the rewrite preserves every signInMessages.<KEY> reference and the .si-error block. Re-scope T-16 to EXTEND SignInMessages.test.tsx (add 'no code path renders NOT_ON_WHATSAPP' and 'no code path renders MISSING_CODE') rather than re-pin strings elsewhere. Add both files to T-25.

findings.title: challengeHandle is now server-minted but still validated as if it were Cognito's Session
findings.problem: The handle changed owner in this design (the browser never sees the Cognito Session; it gets an opaque server-issued handle) but its rule did not: 'opaque server-issued string <= 4096 chars'. §10.1 applies the opposite discipline to the cookie one row above and explains exactly why - a charset/length check before any table read turns a malformed key into a zero-cost rejection rather than a DynamoDB request on a public endpoint with no WAF. POST /customer/session is the busiest unauthenticated route in the feature and challengeHandle is its only lookup key. Three row properties step 5 depends on are also unspecified: the normalized phone (step 6b passes subject=e164 to otp_challenge.verify, and taking it from the body would let a caller pair someone else's handle with their own number), the issuing branch, and a single-use marker.
findings.fix: §10.1: challengeHandle is exactly 43 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-] (secrets.token_urlsafe(32), minted by us); anything else is 400 WITHOUT a table read, same rule and same reason as the cookie. §8.8 step 4: the row is keyed on sha256(handle) (same reason table 1 is keyed on the session-id hash) and carries {handleHash, normalizedPhone, branch in {cognito, phone_ownership}, cognitoAuthSession?, consumed, expiresAtEpoch}, with normalizedPhone read from the ROW and never from the body. Assert both in T-29.

findings.title: Stale line reference for checkout's require_customer call
findings.problem: All three cite ecommerce/checkout/handler.py:196. The call is at :229; line 196 is inside _body. wix-store's :368 is correct. Two of the three citations sit in the paragraphs justifying the method-derived CSRF gate, which is where a reviewer looks first.
findings.fix: Update all three to :229, or cite the function name instead of the line since the tree moves under another session.

findings.title: The KMS statement names an alias where it needs a key ARN
findings.problem: The resource is given as 'the CMK behind alias/wecare-customer-sessions'. An alias ARN is not a reliable resource for kms:Decrypt / kms:GenerateDataKey in an identity policy, and the key ARN is unknown until the provisioning script creates the key.
findings.fix: State that provision_customer_session.py resolves the key ARN from its own CreateKey response (or DescribeKey on the alias) and writes the KEY ARN into both the policy document and REQUIRED_PERMISSIONS, never the alias, so the --verify simulation and the live grant cannot disagree about the resource.

findings.title: /customer/session/echo is an unauthenticated POST with no stated limits and an optional retirement
findings.problem: The echo route answers one question once, yet it is an unauthenticated POST on an API with no WAF, with no throttle named, and --retire-echo is described as something the script can do rather than must do.
findings.fix: State that it performs no table read and no write, that it is subject to the same per-IP otp_throttle axis as /challenge, and that --retire-echo is MANDATORY at §12 step 8 with --verify asserting the route then returns 404. The response shape itself is already correct (booleans plus one four-value enum, no cookie value, no Origin value).

notBlocking.briefCheckList: None of the review brief's enumerated blockers fired. The crux is resolved same-origin with M1 evidence and P1 gating; no token touches localStorage/sessionStorage; CSRF is server-side on every cookie-authenticated mutation including the two DO-NOT-TOUCH handlers via the method-derived flag; the cookie is __Host- on the canonical host and the staff app is excluded by three non-cookie controls; both idle and absolute expiry are server-side and the absolute deadline is pinned three ways and never extended; rotation uses GetTokensFromRefreshToken with a symmetric drift fallback; 5xx/offline/outage is explicitly non-terminal via a four-name allowlist; no mutation derives from a body-selected id; phone ownership is reserved atomically on PHONE#<e164>; the PutItem send-counter rollover finding is present with a code fix and a narrow dedicated-role C-2; X-Forwarded-For stays untrusted; PR #175 is extended additively with no red states, no combined input and no SMS fallback; and no deploy, pool mutation, app-client mutation, WAF, Security Hub or DNS change is proposed.
